column2: adding `step4` to `_commit_route_sites` and calling the shared `_commit_route_run` / `_run_commit_route_leg` path would always invoke `review-and-fix commit-fixes --stage-all`, breaking implementation-specific-files and pathspec-only semantics required for the claude-fallback and recovery commit legs.

folding step 3/4/4.r into one immediate-background `checks-commit-route` launcher removes the foreground step 4 fence that today supplies `implement commit --message` and explicit file pathspecs (or recovery pathspec files). the composite has no pinned argv or tmpdir artifact contract, so ordinary `claude_fallback` runs can stall, commit with empty argv, or invent new semantics.

external no-op vs malformed-manifest recovery (`recovery-commit-message.txt` + `step2-recovery-paths-final.nul`) vs ordinary claude-fallback commit behavior is described in tests and edge cases but not pinned as deterministic selectors in code and skill prose. implementers can pick wrong inputs, commit wrong paths, skip when they should commit, or attempt a second commit on external-complete paths.

current skill requires `implement recovery-paths` after step 3 checks and any checks-repair mutations, then commits via `step2-recovery-paths-final.nul`. folding step 3/4/4.r removes the orchestrator interstitial; the plan edge case names the requirement but does not assign `recovery-paths` between the checks leg and the step4 commit leg inside `checks_commit_route_main`. recovery commits can use stale or missing pathspecs after repair edits.

today `step-2-entry.sh` runs once before the first dispatch. §2.3 q/a cycles re-invoke only `implement run-dispatch` with `--answers`. relocating token/timing marks to `run_dispatch_main` without a once-only guard duplicates step 2 token and timing ledger rows on every resume cycle and skews token reports.
adding the planned retired-scripts row will make `make lint-retired-scripts` flag this fixture, so the slice will fail its own lint gate.

the plan deletes `step2_entry_main`, but `python/test_implement_dispatch.py` still calls it directly. as soon as the symbol disappears, the test fails at runtime before the new launch path is exercised.

the step 6 composite documents non-zero exit with `next_action=continue` for 7.r conflicts and distinguishes seed-failed from checks-failed. the step 3 draft routes generic non-zero to step 18 without the same explicit exception for 4.r conflict relay or `stall_step` assignment.

a branch mismatch still has a valid branch and commit sha, but the wrapper would stop updating `ship-seed-input.env` if persistence is gated only on `post_dispatch_next=continue`. later seeding and stall recovery lose `manifest_path` and `tool_label`.

the plan folds 4.r into the step 3 composite but does not explicitly require rewriting skill macro paragraphs that still say checkpoint 4.r is a direct foreground `push checkpoint-probe` fence. `scripts/test-implement-structure.sh` pins that stale sentence today.

the planned `_run_step4_commit_leg` invokes `implement commit --message-file …`, but `commit_main` only accepts `--message` / `-m` plus optional pathspec flags. recovery and ordinary claude-fallback commit legs will fail at argv parse (usage rc 2) and never commit preserved edits.

the plan says `_run_step4_commit_leg` relays `commit_route_outcome` from `commit_main`, but `commit_main` emits only `committed` / `sha` / `error`. composite callers and tests keyed on `commit_route_outcome` will see missing or malformed envelopes.

inside the composite, `_run_step4_recovery_recompute` scope-check failure is only described as "fail the commit leg closed." today the same failure on `step2-recovery-paths-final.nul` bails to step 12d with `recovery-out-of-scope`. unpinned composite behavior falls into generic `seed-failed` / step 18 `stall_step=4` handling instead of the existing recovery bail cascade.

the plan pins missing-artifact `seed-failed` and step 5/7 `seeded-stall`, but not the path when checks pass and `implement commit` returns non-zero with `committed=false`. orchestrator step 3 post-parse only special-cases `checks-failed`, `stall`, and `continue`; commit failure can be misrouted to step 18, treated as invalid envelope, or proceed to 4.r without a successful implementation commit.

the ordinary claude-fallback wire adds `implementation-commit-paths.nul` but pins no path derivation. without a deterministic source (tracked edit list, `git diff --name-only` against a baseline, or recovery-style recompute), orchestrators can emit empty or stale nul pathspecs; `implement commit --only` then fails or commits nothing after every folded step 3 composite.

`_run_step4_recovery_recompute` is specified without a repo-root input, but `implement recovery-paths` requires `--repo-root`. the malformed-manifest recovery branch cannot recompute `step2-recovery-paths-final.nul` as written; step 4 recovery fails at argument parsing or guesses the wrong repository root.

today manifest-schema-invalid recovery bails at step 2 via `dirty-tree scope-check --paths-file "$recovery_paths_file"` before any composite. the plan only moves post-checks `recovery-paths` + final pathspec scope-check into the composite, so out-of-scope recovery deltas can reach step 3 checks and only fail later.

the new 4.r helper is told to emit exactly one `next_action=continue`, but `checks_commit_route_main` already emits its own `next_action=continue` after the rebase call. that double-print breaks the single-line anchored envelope parse the plan requires.

the plan adds retired rows for both `step-2-entry.md` and `step-2-entry.sh`, but leaves the `.md` file only as an empty updated section and fixes only one retired-path fixture. `make lint-retired-scripts` fails when a retired path still exists, and tracked plan-fidelity fixtures still contain the retired `.sh` path.

the folded step 3→4 composite derives implementation-commit pathspecs via `implement recovery-paths`, which requires a current postlaunch `git status --porcelain` snapshot. today `step2-postlaunch-porcelain.nul` is only written on the `manifest-schema-invalid` recovery path inside `_emit_manifest_invalid_or_recover`; ordinary `status=claude_fallback` exits without creating it. on first composite launch that can yield a missing postlaunch file, empty pathspec, or `seed-failed` despite step 2.4 edits. after step 3 checks-repair main-agent edits, `_run_step4_recovery_recompute` replays the dispatcher-era postlaunch artifact, so recovery commits can omit repaired paths or commit the wrong pathspec.

the plan folds step 3/4/4.r into `checks-commit-route` with post-composite `next_action` parsing, but `skills/implement/skill.md` step 3 still carries a `> **continue after child returns.**` blockquote that routes on `relevant_checks_ok` / `relevant_checks_skipped` and tells the orchestrator to run step 4's commit breadcrumb next. that contradicts the folded composite (which already runs commit + 4.r) and can cause double-commit attempts, skipped 4.r relay, or wrong continuation after repair-loop `continue` before the new parser runs.

`step-2-entry.md` stays listed in the extracted script registry even though the plan deletes the file. that leaves a dead contract in the authoritative skill surface and can keep stale path references alive for linting and readers after the file is gone.

the planned step4 no-op branch returns `commit_route_outcome=noop`, but `commitrouteoutcome` still only allows `continue|seeded-stall|seed-failed`. the new helper signature cannot type-check as written, so pyright or typed tests will fail unless the outcome type is widened; downstream handling and explicit outcome allow-lists can remain inconsistent with the new no-op behavior.

the plan pins step 3 to the new composite launcher, but `checks-repair-loop.md` still omits the full composite argv (including `--rebase-checkpoint-4r`), section 4 retains a step-3-only carve-out that treats `next_action=continue` as checks-only success and forbids re-invoking the capture fence, and line 67 still names `run-step-checks.sh`. after repair-loop main-agent edits, a literal follow can re-launch checks without commit/4.r, commit on a stale branch, or skip 4.r.

the plan rewrites `rebase-checkpoint-routing.md` to fold 4.r into the step 3 composite and updates skill macro text, but `scripts/test-implement-structure.sh` still requires "orchestrator contract — direct probe fences (4.r, 7.r, 7a.r)" in `rebase_ref`. implementing the doc rewrite without updating this needle list fails `make test-implement-structure` or blocks the routing unification.

hoisting step 2 token/timing marks into `run_dispatch_main` does not fully enforce first-dispatch-only telemetry. `step2_dispatch_main` still unconditionally calls `timing mark "step 2 — implementation"` on every external dispatch, including `--answers` q/a redispatch, duplicating ledger rows. the once-only `.step2-telemetry-marked` guard only wraps the wrapper emit and is placed before `dispatch.lock`, so concurrent first dispatches can race, early validation failure can burn the sentinel before the real dispatch runs, and overlapping callers can both write timing rows.

the plan maps `committed=false` to `seeded-stall` + `next_action=stall` and routes the orchestrator with `stall_step=4`, but `_run_step4_commit_leg` does not pin `stall_step="4"` or a dedicated step-4 `bail_reason` / `failure_log_label`. reusing step 5/7 review-fix tokens (e.g. `review-fix-commit-failed`) would misroute `stall_recovery._classify_text` to `step5-review` instead of a post-implementation-commit recovery path. the plan itself never names the step-4 failure token or failure-log label, inviting ad hoc or wrong classification at implementation time.

current recovery sub-branch prose tells the orchestrator to run `implement recovery-paths` and a final scope-check after step 3 checks, then commit in step 4. the plan moves that recompute into `_run_step4_recovery_recompute` but does not explicitly delete the orchestrator block. a literal edit can run recovery-paths twice or leave conflicting step 4 commit instructions beside the folded composite.

`python/cli.py implement recovery-paths` requires `--tmpdir` (`recovery_paths_main` argparse marks it required; tmpdir exclusion in `compute_recovery_paths` depends on it). planned step 2.4 ordinary-fallback and step 4 recovery recompute invocations omit `--tmpdir "$implement_tmpdir"` and/or use bare relative porcelain paths. foreground bash fails argparse (rc 2), mis-includes harness scratch under the repo, or resolves porcelain outside the session tmpdir, leaving `implementation-commit-paths.nul` / `step2-recovery-paths-final.nul` empty and blocking the folded step 3/4 composite. the follow-up `dirty-tree scope-check` also needs an absolute plan path (`"$implement_tmpdir/plan.txt"`) or explicit `cwd=$implement_tmpdir`.

`_write_prelaunch_baseline` runs only on the external-implementer launch path (`step2_dispatch_main` ~2712). pure `status=claude_fallback` (`coder=claude`, missing binary, or `--force`) returns without writing `step2-prelaunch-porcelain.nul` / digests. the plan then derives `implementation-commit-paths.nul` via `recovery-paths` using those missing/empty prelaunch inputs after edits, so pre-existing dirty tracked files can land in the pathspec (empty pre treats every post-launch porcelain entry as new) or `compute_recovery_paths` returns false and the composite hits `seed-failed` with no commit.

the plan adds `--expected-branch` comparison and lists bail on missing match, yet does not require the flag in `step2_post_dispatch_main` argparse or document `required=true` in `step-2-post-dispatch.md`. a partial port can treat omitted `--expected-branch` as "skip compare" and emit `post_dispatch_next=continue` on the wrong branch, weakening the branch-assertion token the issue keeps in orchestrator routing.

on `status=claude_fallback` paths (`coder=claude`, missing-binary, `--force`), `step2-prelaunch-porcelain.nul` and digest artifacts are never written because early branches return before worktree resolution and `run_dispatch_main` calls `_capture_prelaunch_porcelain` without a filesystem `repo_root`. step 2.4 `recovery-paths` and recovery recompute then fail closed or include unrelated pre-existing dirt.

`run_dispatch_main` still exits early when the selected cursor/codex binary is absent, so the planned `status=claude_fallback` path and its prelaunch-capture hook never run for the explicit missing-binary scenario the feature targets.

the plan moves step 3 to `checks-commit-route` with `timeout: 15600000`, but `scripts/test-implement-structure.sh` still requires `skill_text.count('timeout: 10800000') >= 1`. after the fold, skill will have zero `10800000` literals and `make test-implement-structure` fails even when runtime routing is correct.

`run_dispatch_main` is adding a first-dispatch step 2 token row, but codex and cursor launchers still mark the same token on every external run and q/a redispatch, so telemetry will double-count step 2 instead of becoming once-only.
